protocolDescription: Line transect count along two 1-km transects divided into ten 200-m sections. All adult birds seen or heard are recorded by section and by distance band where first noted: 1 (<25 m), 2 (25-100 m), 3 (>100 m, including outside the square) or F (in flight only, any distance). Displaying Skylarks and hovering Kestrels are recorded in a distance band; aerial-feeding Swifts, Swallows and martins are recorded as F unless seen to land. Positively identified juveniles are not counted. No bird is counted twice.
How each bird or group was first detected: S (song), C (call) or V (visual). If used, recorded for all birds on a visit.

Single code per category for overall visit conditions. Cloud 1: 0-33%, 2: 33-66%, 3: 66-100%. Rain 1: none, 2: drizzle, 3: showers. Wind 1: calm, 2: light, 3: breezy. Visibility 1: good, 2: moderate, 3: poor.

Habitat of a 200 m x 50 m strip (25 m either side of the line) per section, recorded separately from bird counts. Up to two habitats per section; per habitat one Level 1 (A-J) and one Level 2 code, up to two Level 3 and two Level 4 codes.

Count all live mammals seen during Early and Late visits (code C). Season presence codes (no counts): D dead, F field signs, L local knowledge, S live animals on additional visits. Observers declare whether they looked for mammals.
Count or estimate the number of pairs of colonially nesting birds (e.g. Rook, Sand Martin) in the whole square, separately from transect counts.
